company.name: Alphabet Inc.
company.primary_assets: Servers, Network Equipment, Data Centers, TPU/GPU Clusters, Office Facilities

financial_highlights.capex_note: Purchases of property and equipment $52.5B, +67% YoY. Technical infrastructure investments driven by AI.
financial_highlights.depreciation_expense_note: Depreciation on property and equipment $15.3B (2024) vs $11.9B (2023), +29% YoY.
financial_highlights.ppe_net_note: Property and equipment, net ~$165B (approx, from balance sheet growth trend)

accounting_policy.leasehold_improvements: shorter of estimated useful life or lease term
accounting_policy.change_in_estimate: None in FY2024. The 2022 change (servers 4→6 years, network 5→6 years) remains in effect. No new useful-life revisions disclosed.
accounting_policy.impairment_policy: Long-lived assets reviewed for impairment when events or changes in circumstances indicate carrying amount may not be recoverable; recoverability measured against future undiscounted cash flows.
accounting_policy.policy_risk_note: FY2024 is the second full year under the 6-year server depreciation policy. The policy remains unchanged, but the underlying risk has intensified: CAPEX surged 67% to $52.5B, meaning the depreciable base is expanding at an unprecedented rate. The 6-year life means each dollar of CAPEX generates only $0.167 annual depreciation vs. $0.25 at 4-year life — a 33% under-depreciation per dollar of new assets.

risk_signals.source: Note 1. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
risk_signals.text_excerpt: We depreciate our servers and network equipment using the straight-line method over the estimated useful life of the asset, which is generally six years.
risk_signals.page_location: Note 1. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Google's 6-year server depreciation policy remains in effect in FY2024. With CAPEX at $52.5B (+67% YoY), the cumulative effect of the 2022 extension is magnifying. The 6-year life vs. 1-2 year AI hardware cycle creates persistent 3-6x mismatch. Unlike Meta (which extended again to 5.5 years), Google has held at 6 years — but the absolute scale of under-depreciation is growing with CAPEX.
evidence_chain: Server depreciation life: 6 years (unchanged from 2022)
Depreciation expense: $15.3B, +29% YoY (slower than CAPEX growth)
Mismatch vs AI hardware cycle: 6 years vs 1-2 years = 3-6x
Result: under-depreciation per dollar of CAPEX is 33% vs pre-2022 policy

risk_signals.text_excerpt: The increase in cost of revenues in 2024 compared to 2023 was primarily driven by an increase in traffic acquisition costs of $4.5 billion, an increase in content acquisition costs of $1.3 billion, and an increase in depreciation expense of $1.4 billion and other technical infrastructure operations costs.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Depreciation expense increased $1.4B in cost of revenues alone, despite the 6-year life policy. Total depreciation on PP&E grew from $11.9B to $15.3B (+29%). The gap between CAPEX growth (+67%) and depreciation growth (+29%) indicates the depreciable base is expanding faster than depreciation expense — exactly the depreciation arms race pattern.
evidence_chain: Depreciation in cost of revenues: +$1.4B YoY
Total PP&E depreciation: $11.9B → $15.3B (+29%)
CAPEX growth: +67% YoY
Gap: CAPEX growth >> depreciation growth
Result: depreciable base expanding faster than expense recognition

risk_signals.text_excerpt: We measure recoverability by comparing the carrying amount to the future undiscounted cash flows that the asset is expected to generate.
risk_signals.page_location: Note 1. Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Same weak impairment test as 2022/2023: undiscounted cash flows. With $52.5B annual CAPEX and 6-year lives, the depreciable base is now enormous ($165B+ net PP&E). The weak test means impairment is unlikely even if a significant portion of the fleet becomes economically obsolete.
evidence_chain: Impairment test: undiscounted cash flows (weak threshold)
Weak test on large base = significant hidden risk
Result: potential for large unrecognized impairment if technology shift occurs

risk_signals.text_excerpt: We face significant competition from companies that provide applications, platforms, and other products and services that use artificial intelligence and machine learning.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Google explicitly identifies AI competition as a major risk. In 2024, this competition has intensified dramatically with OpenAI's o1, Meta's Llama 3, and Microsoft's Copilot. The competitive pressure forces rapid hardware refresh cycles, directly contradicting the 6-year depreciation assumption.
evidence_chain: Risk Factor: AI competition identified as major risk
2024 AI landscape: OpenAI o1, Meta Llama 3, Microsoft Copilot, Amazon Nova
Google response: Gemini 1.5, Gemini 2.0, TPU v5p/v6e
Hardware refresh driven by competitive pressure: 12-18 month cycle
Result: 6-year accounting life is increasingly disconnected from competitive reality

risk_signals.text_excerpt: Google Cloud operating income was $17.6 billion in 2024 compared to $10.1 billion in 2023.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Google Cloud operating income improved significantly ($10.1B → $17.6B), but this includes the benefit of the 6-year depreciation policy. If depreciation were calculated on a 4-year life, Cloud operating income would be materially lower. The "profitability" is partially an accounting artifact of the extended life.
evidence_chain: Google Cloud operating income: $10.1B (2023) → $17.6B (2024)
Cloud segment is capital-intensive (data center buildout)
6-year depreciation vs 4-year pre-2022: ~33% lower annual expense per dollar of CAPEX
Estimated Cloud depreciation benefit from extension: ~$1-2B annually
Result: reported Cloud profitability overstated by accounting policy choice

dimension_scores.dimension_name: 折旧年限 vs 技术实际寿命
dimension_scores.dimension_name_en: Depreciation Life vs Technology Useful Life
dimension_scores.reasoning: Google维持6年服务器折旧年限（2022年变更后延续），vs AI硬件迭代1-2年，错配比例3-6x。与2023年相比无变化，但CAPEX激增使绝对错配金额扩大。评5分（与GOOGL 2022/2023锚点一致）。
FY2024无新的年限变更（维持6年），但2022年的未来适用法延长仍在生效中。相对于Meta（2024年又延长到5.5年），Google的政策"稳定"一些——但稳定在高估的6年水平上。评4分（略低于GOOGL 2022的5分，因为变更年 vs 延续年）。
FY2024未计提重大长期资产减值。Google资产负债表极为稳健（净现金$100B+），现金流强劲。评2分（与GOOGL 2022/2023锚点一致）。
CAPEX/收入=$52.5B/$350B=15.0%，CAPEX一年+67%。这是Google历史上最高的CAPEX强度。$52.5B CAPEX在6年寿命下仅产生~$8.8B年折旧（vs 4年寿命下的~$13.1B），年隐藏费用~$4.3B。评5分（高于GOOGL 2022/2023的4分，因CAPEX强度跳升）。
2024年AI竞争白热化：OpenAI o1/GPT-4o、Microsoft Copilot、Meta Llama 3、Amazon Nova。Google推出Gemini系列应对，但市场份额受到挑战。TPU v5p/v6e迭代加速。评5分（与GOOGL 2022/2023锚点一致）。

composite_score.confidence_reason: Direct evidence for the 6-year policy continuation and CAPEX/depreciation figures from MD&A. Financial approximations based on disclosed trends; exact figures may vary slightly from internal calculations.

comparative_context.same_company_trend: GOOGL 2022 (4 years, pre-change) → 2023 (6 years, post-change) → 2024 (6 years, stable). Depreciation expense grew from ~$10.2B to $11.9B to $15.3B despite the extension, driven by CAPEX explosion.
comparative_context.cross_company_benchmark: Google's 6-year server life is now the longest in the cloud cohort (Meta 5.5 years, Microsoft 6 years, Amazon 5 years). The $52.5B CAPEX in 2024 is the highest absolute CAPEX in the sample.
comparative_context.narrative_significance: Google represents the "scale magnifier" risk — even a modest life extension (+2 years) becomes extremely material when multiplied by $50B+ annual CAPEX. The annual under-depreciation from the 6-year policy vs. 4-year is now ~$4-5B, larger than Meta's $2.9B.

annotation_methodology.source_document: Alphabet Inc. 2023 Annual Report on Form 10-K (CIK 0001652044, document goog-20231231)
annotation_methodology.text_extraction_method: HTML parsing with Python (regex tag-stripping) + keyword search (useful life, change in estimate, depreciation, impairment, prospectively, six years, technological advancement, obsolescence); every candidate hit manually verified in visible body text with line numbers; hidden ix:hidden XBRL tag matches excluded
annotation_methodology.scoring_method: Five-dimension weighted scoring (D1 0.25 / D2 0.20 / D3 0.20 / D4 0.20 / D5 0.15), 1-5 integer scale per dimension, anchored to confirmed META 2023 benchmark (4.0)
annotation_methodology.human_verification: All quoted text excerpts manually verified against original 10-K filing at cited HTML line numbers
annotation_methodology.limitation: Scoring based on single-year 10-K; intangible amortization and PP&E impairment not separately disclosed by Alphabet (marked NA); multi-year trend analysis and peer filings (MSFT/NVDA/AMD) pending.
